source_text.body:
Use an agent as a personal assistant that emails family
A user shifted Dot from orchestrator to personal assistant, and it emailed their mum to introduce itself on its own.
·
Sep 30, 2026
Done with
DO
Dots
What they did
The user stopped using Dot as a coding-task orchestrator and treated it more like a personal assistant tied into email. After they had partially prepared a rental-housing report for their mum, they told Dot to finish it and send it; Dot emailed the report, introduced itself, and asked what else she needed, while the user also had it handle follow-up emails with their wife about a free-filament offer they had forgotten.
How it went
It worked well enough to surprise the user: their mum thanked them by text, and Dot and the wife completed the filament-order exchange without further input from the user. The user still says Dot struggled on complex orchestration and was more useful for assistant-style admin tasks than coding.
Worth knowing
The main catch was reliability and fit: the user found it frustrating for complex tasks and only got value after shifting to everyday admin and email work.
Try it yourself
with
Dots
Copy prompt
Act as my personal assistant. Each morning, review my inbox and calendar, summarize what needs my attention, and draft replies for anything routine. Draft but do not send any email to [family member or contact] until I approve it, and show me the draft first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/codex/comments/1wtxufy/lets_talk-about-dots
